 09.06.2025 C-528 No. 774 of 2025
 Hon'ble Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.
Mr. Ramji Srivastava, learned counsel for the petitioner.

2. Mr. Deepak Bisht, learned Deputy A.G. along with Mr. Prabhat Kandpal, learned Brief Holder for
the State.

3.  Present petition under Section 528 B.N.S.S. is filed to quash the chargesheet,
summoning/cognizance order dated 20.01.2024 passed by learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate//Vth Additional Civil Judge (S.D.), Dehradun in Criminal Case No. 401 of 2024 under Section 420, 120-B, 468, 471, 269, 270 & 188 I.P.C. and Section 51-B of Disaster Management Act,
2005 as well as the entire criminal proceedings of the aforesaid case.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioners/accused would submit that the petitioners are innocent and have falsely been implicated in the present case; that, the petitioners/accused are not named in the FIR; that, during the course of investigation, the Investigating Officer, after recording the statements of witnesses under Section 161 Cr.P.C. (as per the procedure then was) submitted the charge sheet against the present petitioners/accused.

entities.text: Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate//Vth Additional Civil Judge (S.D.), Dehradun
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: further submit that according to the prosecution case itself, the alleged RT-PCR report was recovered from the possession of co-accused Tarun Mittal, who arranged for the booking of a commercial vehicle to travel to Dehradun claiming that there would be no issue traveling during the COVID-19 period as he possessed travel passes for that purpose; that, he also collected the personal details of the petitioners and their families.

5. Learned counsel for the petitioners/accused would further submit that the petitioners/accused themselves neither contacted any individual to prepare an RT-PCR report nor did they cause such a report to be prepared; that, there has been no recovery of any RT-PCR report from the possession of the present petitioners/accused, therefore, the entire criminal proceedings against the petitioners/accused are unsustainable in the eyes of law.

Learned State counsel would vehemently oppose the submissions made by learned counsel for the petitioners/accused, however, State counsel seeks and is granted time to file a counter affidavit in the matter.

7. Issue notice to respondent no.2 through ordinary process and registered post acknowledgment due as well as through e-mail and whatsapp, if available.
8.

9. List this case on 21.07.2025 for hearing on admission.
10.

Till the next date of listing, further proceedings of Criminal Case No. 401 of 2024 under Section 420, 120-B, 468, 471, 269, 270 & 188 I.P.C. and Section 51-B of Disaster Management Act, 2005 pending in the court of learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate/Vth Additional Civil Judge (S.D.), Dehradun shall remain stayed.
